claim: Plasma 6.7 shipped per-screen virtual desktops after 21 years and allows an ICC profile while HDR is active.
quote: After 21 years, hopefully it will have been worth the wait… per-screen virtual desktops have finally arrived! … No longer do you have to choose between color management using an ICC profile or enjoying HDR content; now both are possible at the same time!

claim: Each connected monitor in Plasma 6.7 can show a separate virtual desktop; released June 2026.
quote: Each connected monitor can show a separate virtual desktop. Switching workspaces on one monitor leaves the others untouched.

claim: PlasmaZones is a FancyZones-style KWin zone tiler with 26 built-in layouts and per-monitor/per-desktop layouts, Wayland-only on Plasma 6.
quote: Drag-to-snap tiling with a modifier-held overlay and post-snap zone thumbnails … 26 built-in layouts … Per-monitor, per-desktop, and virtual-screen layouts … KDE Plasma 6 on Wayland — the integration runs as a KWin effect

claim: Plasma 6.7 is the last release that includes an X11 session.
quote: Plasma 6.7 is the last release that will include an X11 session, and it's coming out in just a few days.

claim: Plasma 6.8 (October 2026) drops the X11 session and goes Wayland-only.
quote: KDE Plasma 6.8 Desktop Environment to Drop the X11 Session and Go Wayland-Only

claim: More than 95% of Plasma 6.6 users already run the Wayland session.
quote: KDE Plasma 6.8 Still Planning To End X11 Support, 95% Of Plasma 6.6 Users Are On Wayland

claim: DisplayFusion's feature set includes multi-monitor taskbars, monitor splitting, window position profiles, per-monitor wallpaper, monitor configuration profiles, hotkeys, TitleBar buttons and Triggers.
quote: Keep your windows easily organized by adding a Taskbar to each of your monitors. … divide your monitor into multiple 'virtual' monitors with their own Taskbars, Wallpapers, and Screen Savers. … listen for events, like window creation, window focus, desktop unlock, system idle and more

claim: Fences 6 provides shaded icon groups, automation rules, roll-up mini-windows, Folder Portals and Peek.
quote: Organize your PC by intelligently placing your desktop content into shaded areas called Fence™ groups. … Automatically have files sorted into Fence groups on your desktop with our extensive automation rules … Instantly access your files, folders, and applications with Peek by pressing Winkey + Space

claim: Fences organises desktop icons into moveable groups and can hide icons when not in use.
quote: Fences is a utility for Windows that helps to organize icons on the desktop. It can hide icons when they are not in use as well as make it easy to place icons into moveable groups called "fences".

claim: X-Rite Color Assistant restores Lenovo factory-calibrated ICC profiles (sRGB, HDR, Rec.709) on ThinkPad/Legion panels.
quote: X-Rite Color Assistant enables Lenovo laptop users to restore and manage factory-calibrated ICC color profiles.

claim: KDE's built-in tiling layout editor works like FancyZones but cannot store or swap multiple custom layouts.
quote: you can't save your custom layouts. Whatever layout you choose is preserved indefinitely...but there's no way to easily swap between layouts like in FancyZones.

claim: Tiling Shell brings FancyZones-style layouts, a layout editor and multi-monitor support with differing scale factors to GNOME Shell 42-49.
quote: 🖥️🖥️ multiple monitors support, even with different scaling factors! … ⚙️ Manage, edit, create and delete layouts with a built-in editor

claim: Tiling Shell 17.3 lists GNOME Shell 50 among supported versions.
quote: Version 17.3 (Active) — Shell Versions: 42, 43, 44, 45, 46, 47, 48, 49, 50

claim: Plasma's per-screen task filter exists but stops being honoured after resume from suspend on NVIDIA, requiring a plasmashell restart.
quote: it is possible to fix it by running (after resume from suspend) `systemctl restart --user plasma-plasmashell.service`

claim: Dash to Panel adds a Windows-style taskbar to GNOME with options to isolate running apps by workspace and/or monitor.
quote: This extension moves the dash into the gnome main panel so that the application launchers and system tray are combined into a single panel, similar to that found in KDE Plasma and Windows 7+.

claim: Plasma assigns wallpaper individually per screen; spanning one image across displays is an open request.
quote: its wallpaper handling of multiple displays is that I can only assign a single image or folder to a single display

claim: GNOME still does not support a different wallpaper per screen in 2026; workarounds are manual image compositing or unmaintained extensions.
quote: Feature Request: Per-Screen Wallpaper and Enhanced Slideshow Support

claim: Superpaper is a multi-monitor wallpaper manager for Linux and Windows, with a desktop-environment list rooted in X11-era tooling.
quote: Supported Linux desktop environments / window managers are: BSPWM (needs feh), Budgie, Cinnamon, Gnome, i3 (needs feh), KDE, LXDE & LXQt, Mate, Pantheon, XFCE.

claim: hyprpaper sets wallpapers per monitor by output name in hyprpaper.conf.
quote: wallpaper = <output>,<path> — leave the monitor field empty for a fallback wallpaper

claim: Plasma allows unlimited Folder View widgets on the desktop, each showing a different folder, filterable by regex or file type.
quote: You can put additional Folder View widgets on top of the desktop, or put Folder View in your panel, all of them showing different folders.

claim: Desktop Icons NG supports 'stacking' desktop files, grouping files of the same type, since version 34.
quote: Added support for 'stacking' files, grouping files of the same type

claim: Desktop Icons NG (DING) is the maintained GNOME extension providing desktop icons.
quote: Desktop Icons NG (DING) — Adds icons to the desktop. Fork of the original Desktop Icons extension

claim: DING completed its GTK4 port in v51.0.0, released July 2026, with early GNOME 51 support.
quote: The current version is 51.0.3, with the GTK4 port landing in v51.0.0, released this month, alongside early support for GNOME 51.

claim: Users report there is no way to manually order icons inside a KDE Folder View widget.
quote: I cannot find a way to arrange the order of the icons/shortcuts within the folder view widget.

claim: KWin implements the Wayland session management protocol in Plasma 6.7; toolkit and app adoption is the remaining gate.
quote: KWin now supports the Wayland session management protocol! This is an important step for apps to be able to remember their sizes and positions after restarting the system.

claim: XDG Session Management shipped in wayland-protocols 1.48 on 1 April 2026 and lets clients restore window positions and state.
quote: XDG Session Management allows clients to restore previous window setups, including window positioning and window state.

claim: The RememberWindowPositions KWin script restores window position, size, screen and virtual desktop on Plasma 6+ under both Wayland and X11, with caption-matching and session-restore caveats.
quote: remembers and restores the windows position, size, screen and virtual desktop

claim: The canonical KDE bug about losing window positions when an external monitor is temporarily unplugged is closed as a duplicate of a fixed bug.
quote: RESOLVED DUPLICATE of bug 412703 — Unplugging external monitor repositions windows to right side of screen.

claim: kanshi enables output profiles automatically on hotplug and is the Wayland equivalent of autorandr; it can blank the laptop panel when docked.
quote: kanshi allows you to define output profiles that are automatically enabled and disabled on hotplug ... a Wayland equivalent for tools like autorandr

claim: kscreen-doctor scripts KDE display settings by connector name, and KScreen stores configuration as JSON in ~/.config/kscreen/.
quote: kscreen-doctor manipulates display settings on KDE Plasma, with output IDs that can be numeric (1, 2) or connector names (HDMI-A-1, DP-2)

claim: DisplayCAL, powered by ArgyllCMS, supports X-Rite/Calibrite i1 Display colorimeters and can import vendor colorimeter corrections for i1 Display Pro and ColorMunki Display.
quote: If your measurement device is an i1 Display 2, i1 Display Pro, ColorMunki Display, DTP94, or Spyder2/3/4/5, a popup dialog will show and allow you to import generic colorimeter corrections from the vendor software.

claim: displaycal-py3 is the maintained Python 3 fork of DisplayCAL, targeting Python 3.9+.
quote: DisplayCAL is now working with Python 3.9+

claim: A 2026 Linux calibration walkthrough shows the ArgyllCMS/DisplayCAL loop and warns that applying an ICC profile only inside a colour-managed app does not set the VCGT tables.
quote: applying an ICC profile only to the color managed application is insufficient, because that application won't set the VCGT tables

claim: KDE Plasma on Wayland does not support the API to set VCGT, so calibration curves must be carried in the ICC profile and applied by the CMS instead of the GPU LUT.
quote: KDE Plasma on Wayland doesn't support the API to set VCGT for now

claim: KDE Plasma Wayland gained per-screen colour management, so ICC profiles assigned to each screen work correctly.
quote: Assigning ICC color profiles to each screen will now work correctly under KDE on Wayland.

claim: Plasma 6.7 allows using an ICC profile while HDR mode is active.
quote: You can now use an ICC profile while HDR mode is active!

claim: Wayland's color-management-v1 protocol, covering ICC profiles and HDR, was merged upstream in February 2025 after five years.
quote: After five years in the making and over 800 review comments, Wayland's color-management-v1 protocol is merged to the upstream Wayland Protocols repository.

claim: GNOME 50, released 18 March 2026, added wp_color_management version 2, HDR screen sharing, fractional scaling, VRR and NVIDIA driver-quirk workarounds.
quote: Support for version 2 of the Wayland color management protocol has landed. … Workarounds for NVIDIA driver quirks have been implemented, targeting stuttering and frame-timing issues.

claim: In 2026 every major compositor does per-monitor fractional scaling; KDE allows arbitrary scale values while GNOME is limited to 25% steps, and XWayland apps are rescaled and appear soft with a 5-10% GPU cost.
quote: KDE's edge over GNOME is finer scale steps. You can set any value, like 137% or 163%, while GNOME locks you to 25% steps. … XWayland renders at a single fixed scale, then the compositor rescales for other displays, producing soft text.

claim: Plasma 6.3 reworked fractional scaling for pixel-grid alignment, added panel cloning, and improved colour accuracy with or without ICC profiles.
quote: KWin enhancing the alignment to the screen's pixel grid for sharper images and reduced visual gaps. … Customization options see an update with the ability to clone panels.

claim: A May 2026 field report on NVIDIA 595.71.05 with Plasma 6.6 finds explicit sync removed a class of NVIDIA-specific Wayland glitches, multi-monitor with mixed refresh rates works, VRR may need kscreen-doctor, and open kernel modules are the only option on Blackwell.
quote: Explicit sync landed in Wayland and in KWin. The compositor and the driver now agree on when a buffer is ready to be displayed, removing a category of glitches that affected NVIDIA on Wayland specifically.

claim: NVIDIA 595.58.03 (March 2026) enables nvidia-drm.ko modeset=1 by default and adds DRI3 1.2 with DMA fences.
quote: nvidia-drm.ko modeset=1 parameter is now enabled by default which is essential for Wayland support

claim: The NVIDIA 595 branch raises the minimum supported Wayland version to 1.20.
quote: The NVIDIA 595 Linux driver series bumps the minimum supported Wayland version to 1.20.

claim: GNOME/mutter fails to initialise the NVIDIA dGPU and falls back to CPU rendering when a secondary screen is attached directly to it in hybrid setups; single-display hybrid works.
quote: Secondary GPU initialization failed (Failed to create gbm_surface: Operation not permitted)

claim: External monitors on hybrid NVIDIA+Intel laptops under Wayland are reported as unusable across GNOME, KDE Plasma and Cinnamon.
quote: External Monitor on Hybrid NVIDIA+Intel Laptop on Wayland is unusable

claim: On Lenovo Legion laptops all external outputs (USB-C and HDMI) are wired to the NVIDIA GPU only, and hybrid graphics mode yields a blank external display.
quote: the internal screen is connected to both NVIDIA and AMD GPU, but all external outputs (USB-C and HDMI) are connected to the NVIDIA GPU only ... switching to hybrid graphics mode results in a blank screen in the external output

claim: Lenovo Legion 'Hybrid (iGPU only)' BIOS graphics mode causes its own problems on Linux.
quote: Lenovo Legion 'Hybrid (iGPU only)' setting contaminates linux

claim: KWin's Wayland session automatically enables VRR for fullscreen applications, and unlike X11 multiple monitors do not break G-Sync/FreeSync.
quote: On X11, multiple monitors in a single X display will break G-SYNC/Freesync, however, this problem does not exist on Wayland.

claim: niri treats multi-monitor as core to its design with working mixed DPI and pixel-perfect fractional scaling, and documents no colour management/HDR.
quote: Multi-monitor: yes, a core part of the design from the very start. Mixed DPI works. … Fractional scaling: yes, plus all niri UI stays pixel-perfect.

claim: kanshi defines output profiles enabled and disabled automatically on hotplug for compositors supporting wlr-output-management.
quote: allow you to define output profiles that are automatically enabled and disabled on hotplug

claim: GNOME Shell offers only two multi-monitor workspace modes: workspaces spanning all displays, or workspaces on the primary display only.
quote: Workspaces span multiple displays (which makes it so that multiple displays will show the same workspace always), or Workspaces on primary display only

claim: Independent per-monitor workspaces remain an open feature request in GNOME, not a shipped capability.
quote: Feature Inquiry/Discussion: Independent Workspaces per Monitor (macOS-style)
